issues.summary: The phase registry entry for `dopost-auth-minors` is `"status": "error"` with `failed_at: 2026-08-05T15:12:19` and no `completed_at`, while phases/dopost-auth-minors/index.json has all 5 steps `completed` and the two review-fix commits landed at 16:07/16:16. The registry is stale and misreports a completed phase as failed — a resume or the next session reading phases/index.json first would draw the wrong conclusion (this project has prior incidents of exactly that state-vs-reality drift). Update the entry to completed with a completed_at.

_record_degradation (ingest.py:107-124) re-serializes diagnostics_json with json.dumps but never re-applies runner.truncate_diagnostics_json, so the blob can grow past the 50,000-char Sheets cell cap that truncation exists to enforce. Danger band: a blob already in [~49,860, 49,999] chars (valid JSON, so the ValueError early-return does not fire) plus the ~95-char warning string, the `warnings` list entry and the two new `harness` keys pushes it over 50,000; GAS then throws on the setValues for the pull-marker row, doPost returns result:'error' with no code, _send raises, and the marker is lost entirely. That is the exact combination the code is written for — a pull that went badly (largest blob) during a token outage. Fix: run the final json.dumps back through truncate_diagnostics_json.

On the UNAUTHORIZED path (_send_declared, ingest.py:236-252) _record_degradation unconditionally writes harness.weeks_verified_empty = [], which is only true if NO gated chunk succeeded. If the Script Property is rotated/unset mid-pull, chunk 1 can carry a bypass that GAS accepted before chunk 2 is rejected, and the marker then denies a tombstone bypass that actually happened — the inverse of the honesty guarantee the harness key exists to provide (docstring, ingest.py:90-97). Narrow (needs rotation between chunks of one pull), but cheap to make exact: track the weeks actually accepted and record those instead of [].

PRD-9 (line 25) is still `planned` at HEAD even though every step covering it is completed. PRD.md's own rule directly under the table says to flip planned -> built when the covering phase completes. This was raised in the round-1 review and is still open; TODO.md was updated to say the same work is closed, so the two docs now disagree.

notes: Verified green at HEAD, not taken from the step logs: `node connectors/gas/test_code.js` -> 833 passed, 0 failed; `python -m pytest connectors/shopspend -q` -> 140 passed. (index.json summaries say 827/133 — they predate the two review-fix commits, which added tests.)

TDD audit: all four tdd:true steps (0-3) carry both red and green tdd_evidence in index.json. Step 4 is tdd:false and is genuinely docs-only (TODO.md, docs/api.md, index.json) — no logic in the escape hatch. The two post-phase review-fix commits changed Code.gs and ingest.py outside the step runner, but each shipped tests in the same commit (test_code.js +21, test_ingest.py +206), including the UNAUTHORIZED degradation, the non-UNAUTHORIZED-still-raises case, and a 'stale token value never echoed to stderr' assertion.

Auth surface checked end to end: body.weeks_verified_empty is the single GAS entry point for the breaker bypass (Code.gs:143 gate, Code.gs:251 validation, shopspend.gs:73 consumption) and the gate runs before validateIngest_, so a malformed payload without a token gets 'unauthorized' rather than a validation oracle. checkReadToken_ fails closed when the property is unset. timingSafeEqual_ is correct: on a length mismatch it XORs the caller value against itself, so the loop length tracks the supplied token and never leaks the secret's length. token is never logged, never written to a Sheet column, and is stripped from the payload on the degradation resend.

Boundary check (poster <-> doPost): payload key `token` matches body.token; `code: 'UNAUTHORIZED'` matches err.code in _send/_send_declared; the retry is safe because GAS returns before any write, so the resend cannot double-write rows; the pull marker payload carries no weeks_verified_empty and stays tokenless; `token` is only ever attached when chunk_verified is non-empty, which is unreachable when the credential was falsy (weeks_verified_empty is emptied first), so payload['token'] = None cannot happen. Other connectors (BaseConnector.post) never send the field and are unaffected.

Not a defect, but operational: Code.gs and shopspend.gs changed and the live deployment has not been redeployed in this phase — `bash scripts/deploy.sh` still owes. No ordering hazard either way (an undeployed gate simply leaves the field ungated; a deployed gate with GAS_READ_TOKEN unset locally degrades loudly by design).
